conviction_note: Small positive lean: the July guide's own arithmetic (FY MCR 88.1% vs H1 ~85.3%) implies an H2 MCR near 90.9%, no better than H2 2025 even though H1 2026 ran ~180bp better year on year, and UNH has raised in every 2026 print. But the Street's FY number (~$19.84 = H1 $13.61 + Q3 ~$4.13 + Q4 ~$2.10) already sits in the upper half of $19.50-20.00, the call skew already pays for upside, and the last two raises closed only +1.16% and +0.51%. So p_up is 56 on a 7.0% absolute move (0.84), against a findings sum of +1.0. The two numbers agree in sign and size.
bar: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS ~$4.12-4.15 on revenue ~$111.3-111.4bn: FMP $4.12 (via search snippet, https://site.financialmodelingprep.com/market-news/unitedhealth-q3-earnings-preview-medicare-advantage), $4.15 (https://www.itiger.com/news/1108264915, 2026-10-06; https://www.tikr.com/blog/unitedhealth-stock-is-up-14-in-2026-time-to-sell-or-load-up, updated 2026-09-27). Company FY26 adjusted EPS guide $19.50-20.00 and MCR 88.1% +/-25bp (8-K ex99.1, 2026-07-16). The estimate sources agree, so no cap applies.
positioning_check: Short interest is 15.95m shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, 1.8% of shares outstanding, 3.28 days to cover (equibles.com/stocks/unh/shortinterest, read 2026-10-12, via the sweep row). Not crowded. The 25d skew is -3.93 vol points (calls bid, 'upside paid'), put/call OI is 1.23, and the event-implied move is 6.58%. The stock trades 13.8% below its 52-week high, with a 20-day run-up of -1.97%.

findings.finding: The July guide implies a second half that does not improve on 2025: FY MCR 88.1% +/-25bp against H1 2026 ~85.3% implies H2 ~90.9%, versus H2 2025 ~90.7% (Q3 2025 89.9%, Q4 2025 adjusted 91.5%), although H1 2026 ran ~180bp better year on year (Q2 -270bp). UNH has raised in every 2026 print (Jan >$17.75, Apr >$18.25, Jul $19.50-20.00), so another raise is likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide raised: Apr 2026 +6.96%, Jul 2026 +1.16% close (faded from about +8.8% intraday per the sweep), Oct 2025 +0.51%. Guide cut or withdrawn: Apr 2025 -22.38%, and Jan 2026 -19.61% on the initial 2026 guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The Street's FY sum (~$19.84) already sits in the upper half of the guide, and calls are bid. If a raise to ~$20.25+ were fully priced, the stock would not sit 13.8% off its high on a -2% 20-day run-up, and Q4 consensus (~$2.10, flat on $2.11) would not be the only declining quarter. The H2 MCR arithmetic against H2 2025 does not appear in the previews I found, which focus on the Q2 reserve release.
findings.independence: The Q3 2025 MCR of 89.9% is from the Q3 2025 release (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20251028682656/en/UnitedHealth-Group-Reports-Third-Quarter-2025-Results-and-Raises-Full-Year-2025-Earnings-Outlook). The Q4 2025 adjusted MCR of 91.5% and FY 89.1% are from https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/2823631/unitedhealth-q4-earnings-beat-on-strong-optum-rx-offers-2026-outlook. The Q4 consensus of ~$2.10 is from https://www.tikr.com/blog/unitedhealth-trades-at-365-as-it-shuts-plans-for-390000-medicare-advantage-members-heres-what-it-signals-for-2027. This shares the 2026-07-16 release with the reserve finding below.

findings.finding: Reserves carry cushion into Q3: Q2 2026 had $860m of net favorable development, mostly on 2026 dates of service, and days claims payable rose to 47.0 from 44.5 a year earlier (48.6 in Q1). Conservative H1 reserving makes further favorable development, or a lower Q3 MCR than modelled, more likely than an adverse true-up.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 EPS beat (~$1.50 over ~$4.9, helped by the $860m release) closed only +1.16%. The Q1 2026 beat ($7.23 vs ~$6.5-6.6) closed +6.96%.
findings.why_not_priced: The previews treat the $860m as a one-off that flatters Q2 and should not repeat, which caps Q3 consensus at ~$4.13. If the market read it as a sign of conservative reserving, Q3 numbers would have drifted up after July. The FY consensus moved only from $19.71 (July) to $19.69 (August), per MarketBeat reprints.
findings.independence: Same document as the guidance finding: two readings of one release, sized small for that reason. The FY consensus drift is from https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/fy2026-earnings-estimate-for-unh-issued-by-zacks-research-2026-08-03/.

findings.finding: At the Wells Fargo conference on 2026-09-09 (8-K item 7.01 of 2026-09-08), the CFO reportedly said Medicaid margins sit at the better end of the -1% to -1.7% range, that MA margins are tracking the upper half of 2-4%, and that the guide stands.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No history for a mid-quarter reaffirmation in the baseline. The stock is -1.97% over 20 days since.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it was a public webcast and it lands inside the guided range. It is kept as a small positive because a CFO pointing to the better end of segment ranges five weeks before quarter-end is consistent with a raise, and Q3 consensus has not moved toward that.
findings.independence: The 8-K confirming the appearance is https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000731766/000073176626000205/unh-20260908.htm (no text of the remarks in it). The quotes come from a third-party blog only.

findings.finding: Hospital counterparties reporting after UNH's July print saw moderate, not hot, utilization: HCA Q2 same-facility admissions +2.5% with inpatient surgeries -2.3% and outpatient surgeries -3.4%; Tenet Q2 admissions +2.3% with surgeries -0.7%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: UNH's MCR line: improvements in 2026 were paired with +6.96% and +1.16%, and the 2025 MCR blowouts with -22.38% and -19.61%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a proxy for Q2, a period UNH had already reported, so it is largely priced. It is kept only because it is independent confirmation that utilization was not re-accelerating going into Q3. No Q3 hospital series was found.
findings.independence: Tenet Q2 2026 release: https://investor.wedbush.com/wedbush/article/bizwire-2026-7-23-tenet-reports-strong-second-quarter-2026-results-raises-2026-financial-outlook (2026-07-23). This is a proxy, not company-level data.

findings.finding: The 2027 MA posture will be argued on the call: UNH's share of members in 4+ star plans for 2027 (payment year 2028) fell to ~67% from 78% (Stephens via Fierce; CMS released 2026-10-08; UNH says it is 'consistent with expectations'), and UNH is shutting plans covering ~390,000 MA members for 2027 (company spokesperson to Bloomberg, 2026-10-01). Commentary on 2027-2028 MA revenue and membership is the likely drag on any raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Initial forward-year guide (Jan 2026) -19.61%. The April 2026 final 2027 MA rate notice (+2.48%) moved the stock about +10% intraday per Yahoo.
findings.source_date: 2026-10-08 (CMS release date; page returned 403 to fetch, so the figures are from the search snippet only)
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: both items are public and the stock rose from ~$365 (2026-10-02) to $376. It stays a small negative because neither the 2028 star-bonus headwind nor the 2027 membership loss has been quantified by the company. A first 2027 frame on the call could anchor down, and the call-side skew says the market is not positioned for that.
findings.independence: The 390k figure is from https://www.tikr.com/blog/unitedhealth-trades-at-365-as-it-shuts-plans-for-390000-medicare-advantage-members-heres-what-it-signals-for-2027 (updated 2026-10-02). baseline_tension: The findings lean the same way as the call skew (-3.93, upside paid), so most of the positive is likely already in the price. The flat 20-day run-up and the 13.8% gap to the 52-week high leave room. The name's habit of fading beat-and-raise prints (+1.16%, +0.51%) is what keeps p_up near 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name faded its last two raises at +1.16% and +0.51%): guidance finding 1.5 -> 1.0, reserve finding 0.5 -> 0.3, p_up 57 -> 56.
Rule 6 (inside what the company guided): Wells Fargo reaffirmation 0.3 -> 0.1. Bar checked against two agreeing sources ($4.12/$4.15), so no cap.
Rule 5 (proxy): hospital Q2 volumes 0.2 -> 0.1, as a proxy for a quarter UNH had already reported.
Rule 7: short interest 1.8% / 3.3 days, not crowded. The negative MA-2027 finding was left at -0.5 because it is already small against the call skew.

Rule 3: read the findings as a set. The guidance and reserve findings share one document; the reserve finding stays small rather than being merged, because it is a different fact (reserves vs guide math).
